Who are the Azande?

Who are the Azande?

The Azande (also written Zande) live in three countries: South Sudan, DR Congo and the Central African Republic. The name means "the people who possess much land." We speak Pa-Zande, which has about 1.1 million speakers, and share one culture across these borders. Estimates of our population vary; one common figure is about 3.8 million.

South Sudan

Western Equatoria State.

DR Congo

The north-east, along the Uele River.

Central African Republic

The south-east, around Rafaï, Zemio and Obo.

Our history

The Azande came together in the 1700s when warrior clans expanded and joined neighbouring groups under one language and way of life. The Avongara clan became the ruling nobility.

1700s
The Bandia and Avongara dynasties expand and unite many groups as the Azande.
1870 to 1905
King Gbudwe rules. He is killed in February 1905 while resisting British rule.
Colonial era
The kingdoms are ended, but the Avongara lineage continues.
9 February 2022
The monarchy is restored. King Atoroba Peni Rikito Gbudue takes the throne after 117 years.

Our King

His Majesty King Atoroba Peni Rikito Gbudue leads the restored Azande Kingdom. The lion on his hat and the blade on his robe are symbols of the kingdom.

Our elders

The King is supported by the elders of the community, men and women, who keep our customs alive.

Our culture

Dress, music, food, farming and craft: this is how the Azande live.

Traditional wear

Orange and copper cloth, cowrie-shell necklaces and headbands, fibre trims and woven hats.

Music and dance

Wooden gongs, drums and the sansa thumb piano carry our songs. Storytelling is central, including the trickster tales of Ture.

Traditional food

Cassava, millet and groundnuts are staples. A thick porridge is served with a meat or vegetable sauce. Termites are a favourite.

Farming

The Azande are mainly small-scale farmers. The King and elders lead by example.

Hunting

Hunting is also part of traditional life.

Tools and craft

The Azande were skilled metalworkers. We also make pottery, carved wooden utensils, baskets and mats.

Traditional marriage

Marriage is celebrated in traditional dress with decorated gourds.

Where we live

South Sudan

Yambio, Maridi and Tombura, in Western Equatoria.

DR Congo

Bas-Uele and Haut-Uele, including Isiro and Dungu.

Central African Republic

Rafaï, Zemio and Obo.

Questions

Who are the Azande?

A people who speak Pa-Zande and live in South Sudan, DR Congo and the Central African Republic.

What does Azande mean?

"The people who possess much land."

Who is the King?

King Atoroba Peni Rikito Gbudue, enthroned on 9 February 2022 when the kingdom was restored.

Who was King Gbudwe?

The Azande king who ruled from 1870 to 1905 and was killed in 1905 resisting British rule.
